correctness.rationale: The proof is an exact two-way reconstruction. Coprimality of the target with the differentiated prime product forbids every active exponent at least two; the surviving exponent-one support \(T\) gives \(D_S(mP_T)=mH(T)\), and \(H(T)\mid y\) is sufficient as well as necessary. Distinct \(T\) give distinct preimages. The minimum and maximum arguments then follow exactly. A finite regression program checks 135 coprime targets across four prime sets but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The coprime-target slice is intrinsic: it is exactly the target condition that collapses differentiated-prime exponent vectors to squarefree active subsets. The theorem completely solves the inverse problem on that stratum for every finite \(S\), supplies exact fiber cardinalities and extremal branching, and directly advances the finite-set anti-derivative direction identified by the motivating 2022 paper.
